topic: What link budget trade-offs exist when balancing data rate and reliability in adverse weather for satellite backhaul links?
consensus_response: The physical mechanism of atmospheric attenuation at W-band frequencies (71-76 GHz) dominates gas absorption, rain, and clouds. High transmission powers (>50W) are required to compensate, increasing cost in terms of power consumption and heat dissipation. Advanced modulation schemes or error correction codes can mitigate rain fade effects but introduce complexity and potential interference. Beamforming can potentially improve signal quality and reduce transmission power requirements, but it also introduces new challenges.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the impact of atmospheric attenuation on satellite backhaul links, particularly at W-band frequencies (71-76 GHz), requiring high transmission powers to compensate for signal loss due to gas absorption, rain, and clouds. This affects link reliability and performance.
